transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
No matter how much I rest, I feel completely drained and can’t keep up or focus at work anymore. It's just gotten to the point where I'm really struggling to get through my shifts.
Did these symptoms start after a specific stressful life event or major change, or did they come on without any clear trigger? If there was a stressor, what was it and when did it happen?

It all started about two years ago when my clinic did a major electronic health record upgrade right as I started evening classes for my LPN. Between studying, working, and picking up extra shifts because of staffing shortages, the pressure just gradually became too much to handle.

Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down or hopeless most days, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy? Or does it feel more like exhaustion and being overwhelmed from the ongoing stress?

It is definitely both. I wake up almost every day with a heavy, sinking sadness like a dark cloud on my chest, and I’ve completely lost interest in hobbies like jogging or my Raspberry Pi projects. While I am physically exhausted and feel like my body is made of concrete, this goes way beyond normal work stress—it's a deep, constant feeling of hopelessness.

If your work and school stress were reduced or removed, do you think the sadness and loss of interest would mostly go away, or would they still be there on their own? Have these symptoms ever continued even during breaks or less stressful periods?

I think they would still be there on their own now. Even on my days off when I try to rest and there's no immediate stress, that heavy, hopeless feeling and exhaustion don't lift at all. It really feels like the sadness and lack of energy have taken on a life of their own.

Over the past two weeks, have you been having strong feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt nearly every day? If so, does that feel out of proportion to the work and school stress you've been under?

Yes, I feel like a terrible nurse's aide and just a bad person almost every day. I've convinced myself that every small charting error or forgotten vital sign means I'm putting patients at risk on purpose and deserve to be punished. It definitely feels way deeper and more severe than just typical stress from work and school.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, that you’d be better off dead, or of hurting yourself? If yes, have you thought about how you would do it or made any plans?

On my worst days, I do catch myself thinking it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. I've pictured a couple of times what it would be like to drive my car off the highway on the way home from a shift. But I haven't made any concrete plans or taken any steps to actually do it.

When you feel that you deserve to be punished or are putting patients at risk, do you know these are thoughts from depression, or do you actually believe them as facts? Have you also heard or seen things others don’t, or felt certain that people are watching, judging, or trying to punish you?

To me, those feelings are absolute facts, and I'm convinced the new charting system was designed specifically to track my mistakes and get my license pulled. I also pretty often hear a low male voice right behind me when I'm alone or on late shifts, telling me that I'm screwing up or that they know I'm dangerous.

Before this episode that began about two years ago, had you ever had another separate period lasting at least two weeks when you felt similarly depressed or lost interest in things, especially if it got better in between? Or has this been the first and only episode like this in your life?

No, this is the first and only time in my life I've ever felt like this. Before these past two years, I was doing really well, managing my busy schedule, jogging, and working on my hobbies. This heavy depression and these overall struggles are completely new to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a first major depressive episode with persistent depressed mood, marked anhedonia, fatigue, hopelessness, excessive guilt/worthlessness, and suicidal ideation. Psychotic features are present and mood-congruent, including fixed guilt/persecutory delusional beliefs about being dangerous and targeted by the charting system, plus auditory hallucinations criticizing the patient. Symptoms have persisted independently of stressors, and there is no history of prior episodes provided.
